quandoUsar: A single value against a known range on a dashboard: server load, support score, quota usage.
When the value has named states (healthy, busy, critical): with `thresholds`, color and label change the instant the number crosses each limit.
quandoEvitar: Use `progress` for the progress of a task with a known end, such as a file upload.
Use `usage-meter` when it matters to see what fills a quota and how much remains before the limit.
Use `slider` when the user needs to adjust the value; the gauge is read-only.
acessibilidade: The ring is a `role="meter"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, and an `aria-valuetext` with the percentage and the band name; the drawing and the animated number are `aria-hidden`.
Each `thresholds` band has a text `label`, so the state doesn't depend on color alone.
`label` is required; the figure's `aria-label` joins label, value, and maximum with a fixed English “of”.
movimento: The first fill waits until half of the gauge enters the viewport: the arc closes slowly, without overshooting the value, while the number counts up.

On each new value, the arc and number move there on a spring; the band's color and label change when the on-screen number crosses the limit, and the text enters from below if the value rose or from above if it fell.
With “reduced motion”, the arc and number jump to the value and the texts swap with a quick fade.
responsivo: The ring takes `min(100%, 176px)` of width and the stroke thickness scales with it; there is no size prop, so the parent's width decides.
notasIA: The center always shows the percentage within the range (`7.4` between 0 and 10 appears as 74%), not the raw value; use `detail` to state the value with its unit.
In `thresholds`, the band with the highest `from` that the value reaches applies: include one with `from` equal to `min` so there is always a state; without `thresholds`, the color comes from `tone`.
It accepts neither `className` nor a size: wrap it in a container with the width you want, remembering that the ring doesn't exceed 176 px.
